name: Epitalon

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Mouse, rat, monkey and cell studies, mostly 1 group

track.title: Pilot in people

track.title: FDA approval

what.text: Epitalon, also spelled epithalon, is a chain of four amino acids: Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly. Its molecular weight is about 390 daltons. It is sold as a free base or an acetate salt. It is a common name, not an official drug name.

It was made as a synthetic copy based on epithalamin, an extract of cattle pineal gland, and appears to have first been synthesized in 1999. FDA treats epitalon and epithalamin as different substances, although sellers often use the names interchangeably.
Most of the research comes from one group in St. Petersburg, Russia, led by Vladimir Khavinson, and its collaborators.
How it acts, according to animal and cell studies:

items.text: In human fetal lung cells in the lab, it switched on telomerase and lengthened telomeres, the protective caps on chromosomes.

src.label: Khavinson et al., Bull Exp Biol Med, 2003

items.text: In old female rhesus monkeys, 10 days of injections raised evening melatonin and restored the day-night rhythm of cortisol. It had no effect on melatonin in young monkeys.

src.label: Goncharova et al., Bull Exp Biol Med, 2001

items.text: In rat pineal glands in the lab, it did not raise melatonin release directly. How it changes melatonin is unknown.

what.text: None of these mechanisms has been confirmed in people.
Adonis does not carry epitalon today.

research.text: Human evidence is thin and almost all from Russia. FDA found three studies that gave epitalon to people and none that assessed its safety. Most animal and cell studies come from a single St. Petersburg research group.

research.title: Melatonin in night-shift workers, 2021

facts.v: Ivko et al. 2021, as summarized by FDA
randomized, placebo-controlled. Blinding was not described.
75 healthy women aged 40 to 50, mostly night-shift workers. 40 with low melatonin output were split between epitalon and placebo; 35 with normal output served as a comparison.
an under-the-tongue spray (a French product), or a salt-water placebo
20 days
a melatonin breakdown product in urine, and clock genes in blood cells

research.found: The melatonin product rose 1.7-fold on epitalon and did not change on placebo. Sleep was not measured. No safety data were reported. FDA noted the small size and short length.

research.title: Retinitis pigmentosa, 2002 (Russia)

facts.v: Khavinson V, et al. Neuro Endocrinol Lett 2002;23(4):365-8
a rat study and a patient study, reported together; PubMed lists it as a controlled clinical trial
patients with inherited retinal degeneration; the abstract gives no count
injection next to the eye (parabulbar), per FDA
retinal condition

research.found: The authors report a positive clinical effect in 90% of cases. The abstract gives no numbers of patients or details of the control group.

src.label: Khavinson et al., Neuro Endocrinol Lett, 2002

items.text: Khavinson et al. 2021 gave under-the-tongue epitalon to night-shift workers to study circadian genes. FDA lists it but reports no results.

a 2007 abstract (Korkushko et al.) says pineal preparations had "no side effects" in elderly people, with no route, dose, length, numbers or methods given. FDA could not evaluate the full paper, which is in Russian.

research.text: Registered trials with no results yet

research.title: Topical peptide serum and aging clocks

facts.v: NCT07888595, sponsored by Frontiers in Bioscience Research Institute and Aging
single group, open-label; untreated skin areas on the same person serve as controls
about 48 healthy adults aged 50 or older planned
4 weeks for the main measure
gene- and protein-based "biological age" in skin and blood

research.found: Epitalon is one of five peptides in a skin serum, given alongside other agents such as metformin. The design does not test epitalon alone. First posted October 2026; enrolling by invitation.

research.title: Lifespan and tumors in female mice, 2003

facts.v: Anisimov VN, Khavinson VKh, et al. Biogerontology 2003;4(4):193-202
controlled animal study, epitalon against saline
54 female Swiss-derived SHR mice per group
under-the-skin injections 5 days each month, from 3 months of age until natural death
lifespan, tumors, chromosome damage, aging markers

research.found: No change in mean lifespan, food intake or body weight. Maximum lifespan was 12.3% longer, and the last 10% of survivors lived 13.3% longer. Total tumor rate did not change; leukemia was less common.

research.text: The same group reported similar lifespan and tumor studies in other mouse strains. FDA notes that they used one fixed dose, only female mice, and short total exposure (at most about 22 weeks in the 2003 study). Animal results have not been confirmed in people.

items.text: FDA’s scientists, in a memo dated May 12, 2026 for the July meeting, recommended against adding epitalon (free base or acetate) to the compounding list. They evaluated it only for insomnia and found no studies in people with insomnia, no human safety data, and no studies of the injected route proposed.
Anti-aging, longevity, telomere lengthening and other proposed uses were not evaluated, because the nominations did not include enough information.
FDA’s advisory committee was asked to vote on both forms on July 24, 2026.

us.text: Not FDA-approved for any use. Since October 30, 2026, HHS has said it will not take enforcement action against licensed pharmacies and physicians that compound Epitalon acetate for injection under the skin or into muscle, dispensed in intermittent courses, under set conditions. That is enforcement discretion, not approval. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: none. Epitalon has no USP or National Formulary monograph and is not a component of any FDA-approved drug.
FDA granted an orphan drug designation for retinitis pigmentosa on September 2, 2010, and it was withdrawn or revoked on January 6, 2016. A designation is not an approval.

FDA lists epitalon among substances previously in Category 2 whose nominations were withdrawn. FDA wrote that it found no safety information for the proposed route and cannot know whether it would cause harm in people.
Wells Pharmacy Network and LDT Health Solutions (for the International Peptide Society) nominated it; both withdrew. FDA reviewed it on its own initiative.

HHS announced an enforcement discretion policy on October 28, 2026, published in the Federal Register on October 30, 2026 (Docket HHS-OASH-2026-0496). It names Epitalon acetate, for injection under the skin or into muscle, dispensed in intermittent courses. HHS says it does not intend to take enforcement action against state-licensed pharmacies, federal facilities or licensed physicians that compound it when every condition is met. As of October 31, 2026.

src.label: HHS notice, Federal Register 2026-22192 (Docket HHS-OASH-2026-0496), signed by Secretary Kennedy, filed Oct 28, 2026
BakerHostetler summary of the HHS policy (a law firm's summary, used because HHS's own policy appendix could not be opened)

items.text: a licensed pharmacist or physician compounds it; the bulk substance matches the listed peptide and route; it comes from an FDA-registered maker that follows good manufacturing practice, with a valid certificate of analysis; there is a valid patient-specific prescription; the product contains only one active ingredient from the list; serious adverse events and quality problems are reported to FDA's MedWatch and state authorities; the label says "This is a compounded drug product. Not for resale."; oral forms have documented adequate bioavailability; the only device packaged with it is an FDA-cleared syringe; and all other section 503A requirements are met.

src.label: BakerHostetler summary of the HHS policy (a law firm's summary, used because HHS's own policy appendix could not be opened)

items.text: The policy does not make it FDA approved. It does not cover blends with other active ingredients, other routes or forms, outsourcing facilities (section 503B), or products sold as research chemicals or dietary supplements. It is interim and not binding: HHS may revise or withdraw it, in whole or in part, if safety signals or product-quality problems appear.

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

world.lead: No regulator has approved epitalon. Canada names it among seized unauthorized peptides. FDA’s 2026 search found no approved product in Canada, Australia, the UK or several EU countries, and none authorized by EMA.

countries.status: Not approved. Compounding under HHS enforcement discretion since Oct 30, 2026, for Epitalon acetate by injection under the skin or into muscle, dispensed in intermittent courses only.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Epitalon is not named on the WADA Prohibited List for 2026 or 2027. WADA’s class S0 bans at all times any pharmacological substance with no current approval by any government health regulator for human use. For 2027, WADA added "peptides" as an example in S0 and warned that a peptide not named on the List may still be prohibited. The lists do not say whether epitalon falls under S0.

side.text: FDA found no clinical studies of epitalon’s safety in people and no human pharmacokinetic data. Its risks in people are unknown, and FDA raised a theoretical cancer concern.

items.text: the 20-day spray study reported no safety data. A 2007 abstract claimed "no side effects" without details.
FDA’s adverse event database (through December 8, 2025) and its food and supplement complaint system (through December 5, 2025) held no epitalon reports.

FDA writes that epitalon "has the potential to be carcinogenic", because it is reported to switch on telomerase and lengthen telomeres, and long telomeres are linked with higher cancer risk. No 2-year cancer studies exist. The mouse tumor studies were too short and limited to settle this.
no single-dose, repeat-dose or reproductive studies were found. Small fixed-dose mouse studies showed no rise in chromosome damage.
FDA is concerned about immune reactions to injected epitalon from clumping and peptide impurities.
Health Canada warns that unauthorized injectable peptides may hold the wrong amount of ingredient or contaminants.

unconfirmed: FDA’s record of the July 24, 2026 advisory committee vote on epitalon was not found among the meeting materials, so the vote result is left out.
FDA’s orphan designation database showed a bot check and could not be opened; the 2010 designation and 2016 revocation come from FDA’s briefing only.
The 2021 studies by Ivko et al. and Khavinson et al. were not found on PubMed and were not opened; they are reported as FDA summarized them.
UK, EU-country and Australian status rest on FDA’s 2026 search, not on MHRA or TGA records; epitalon’s status in Russia was not checked.
surprises: Epitalon is sold as a telomerase activator and "fountain of youth", but FDA cites that same telomerase effect as a reason it may have cancer potential, and no long-term cancer studies exist.
Websites say it extends lifespan, but in the main mouse study mean lifespan did not change; only maximum lifespan and the longest-lived 10% did.
Sellers list epithalamin as another name for epitalon; FDA treats them as different substances.
FDA could evaluate epitalon only for insomnia; claims for anti-aging and longevity had too little information to evaluate.
Products are often labelled "for research use only" while being marketed for human use, a label Health Canada says does not make them legal.
